answer_key_points: The optional WITH clause specifies storage parameters for the index; each index method has its own set of allowed storage parameters, and the B-tree, hash, GiST and SP-GiST index methods all accept fillfactor.

The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages; for B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds and when extending the index at the right, and B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90 (any integer from 10 to 100 can be selected).
B-tree indexes on tables with many anticipated inserts or updates can benefit from lower fillfactor settings, while a fillfactor of 100 should only be considered for a completely static table.
